root_cause.text: An off-by-one bounds check in `drivers/input/touchscreen/ti_am335x_tsc.c:titsc_config_wires()` validated `wire_order[i]` with `>` instead of `>=`, allowing the invalid index `ARRAY_SIZE(config_pins)` to pass and be used for out-of-bounds access to `config_pins`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `if (WARN_ON(wire_order[i] > ARRAY_SIZE(config_pins)))` to `if (WARN_ON(wire_order[i] >= ARRAY_SIZE(config_pins)))`, and the CVE/commit text explicitly states that allowing `wire_order[i] == ARRAY_SIZE(config_pins)` causes out-of-bounds access when indexing `config_pins[wire_order[i]]`.

bic_trace_step.reason: The relevant logic is fully shown in `titsc_config_wires()`, so the snippet is sufficient. The vulnerable construct is present in the bounds check: `if (WARN_ON(wire_order[i] > ARRAY_SIZE(config_pins))) return -EINVAL;`. Since `config_pins` has 4 elements (`static const int config_pins[] = { ... };`), valid indices are `0..3`, but this check only rejects values greater than 4. A value equal to `ARRAY_SIZE(config_pins)` (that is, `4`) incorrectly passes. That value is then used directly as an array index in `bit_cfg = config_pins[wi_order];`, producing an out-of-bounds access. The fix would require rejecting `wi_order >= ARRAY_SIZE(config_pins)`, but this code still uses `>`, so the fix is not present.
